_comment: REQUIRED BY DEFAULT. A registered type binds on EVERY action unless an entry says otherwise, and saying otherwise costs a stated `reason`. The minimal entry {"family": "..."} is the STRICT one -- adding a type is one line and it binds immediately. Inclusion is free; exclusion is the thing that takes effort.
_why: The first draft listed required steps explicitly per action, so adding a checker meant writing it AND remembering to add it to the list. Forget the second half and the checker runs, passes, and counts for nothing -- absence rendering as success, in the very file that defines what complete means. A registry you must remember to extend is a registry that will be incomplete.
_reasonless_narrowing: An `actions` or `when` narrowing with NO `reason` is IGNORED and the type falls back to required-for-all. This is the encoding_whitelist.txt convention, reused deliberately because it is already familiar here: nothing is suppressed until a human has actually looked. A typo in an exemption fails safe.
_unregistered: V8 rejects a record whose step is not listed here, record.py returns None, and the checker exits 2 -- so the pipeline blocks the moment someone wires in an unregistered check, loudly, at the desk of the person who can fix it. That is the pair that closes the hole: you cannot add a check that silently does not count, and you cannot register one that silently is not required.

genesis.reason: the recording floor itself; it is not a gate on any action

editorial.reason: the published prose surface. The exclusions are policy, not tidying: CLAUDE.md exempts tools/verify/** and tools/process/** from both prose gates (/rely covers those instead), and ZeroParadox/*.md are ride-along docs beside their .lean, reviewed as corpus rather than as publications. CLAUDE.md itself is excluded for the same reason it names -- operating machinery that asserts nothing about the mathematics, so editorial and adversary have no claim on it. .claude/commands/*.md is IN scope by CLAUDE.md R-EXEMPT: the gate briefs are published deliberately, as the artifact showing how this project reviews itself, so both prose gates fire on them; published-and-exempt is not a category to reason into. The blanket `.claude/*.md` exclusion was removed on 2026-08-25 because it silently cancelled that -- `*` DOES cross `/` here (measured: check_encoding's scope ["*"] covers 450 tracked files), so the blanket entry matched every brief under commands/. `*.html` was added 2026-08-29: the three interactive maps (bottom-family-tree, diagonal-family, snap-loop) are PUBLISHED and linked from README and GUIDE, and were in NO gate's scope until then -- `inventory` listed snap-loop.html under subjects_unscoped for adversary, editorial AND claim_review. The cost was measured, not argued: bottom-family-tree.html carried, twice, a citation R-BEDROCK prohibits in terms (`rInv_swaps` credited for a COINCIDENCE, when it proves an EXCHANGE between provably distinct points) while its .md sibling was corrected the same day, because nothing looked at it. `_layouts/*` is excluded because the Jekyll layout is chrome -- CSS and one routing comment, no mathematical content -- and it is excluded BY PATH rather than by narrowing the glob, so a new .html at the root falls INTO scope rather than silently out of it; same direction check_encoding's reason states for the same argument. ⚠ These are reviewed by AGENT and deliberately NOT by a glyph checker: the HTML entity-encodes every math symbol, so check_poles scores ZERO on these files and ELEVEN after decoding, and only 2 of those 11 were defects -- the other 9 are the ratified naming idiom, and the discriminator (swaps versus coincide) is semantic.

It is registered so that a CLEAN run leaves a record - verdictLedger.md section 2, 'a step that passes MUST emit a record; silence is never a pass' - which names this file as the measured instance of the defect. Its verdict is honest (it records what it found) and its status is non-gating, which is the registry/admission split working as designed.

check_fields.reason: ADVISORY reading list, registered so it can RECORD but gating nothing. Its JUDGEMENT half is computed from the Lean - it resolves each `field := binding` in every instance to a theorem or a def - and cannot be wrong. Its ENUMERATION half is a text scan over prose blocks and can be, so CLAUDE.md rung 5 applies: the screen may replace the enumeration, never the verdict. Registered 2026-08-26 after /rely RLY35-3: unregistered meant V8 refused every record, `--record` exited 2 for ever, and run_field_discipline turned that into a printed WARN while precommit still said PASS - a checker that runs, costs time, and can never leave a key, which is the exact 'silence is never a pass' defect one layer over.

check_claude_md._min_coverage_why: Pinned 2026-09-18 on Tim's ruling; this step sits at exactly 100% of its declared scope at the live tip, and the pin is recorded so a later drift is a decision rather than a silent slide. ⚠⚠ READ WHAT THE BAR ACTUALLY MEASURES BEFORE CITING IT. `inventory.py` computes the denominator as `scope INTERSECT changed`, NEVER the whole scope. So this pin does NOT block a step that drifts to 90% of its declared scope -- that case still reads SATISFIED -- and it does NOT fire on a commit touching nothing in scope, which takes the `continue` branch and passes at any coverage. An earlier version of this note claimed both, and was FALSE. Corrected by /rely 2026-09-18 (B1), which read the MECHANISM rather than the rationale sitting beside it. ⛔ AND THE PIN REMOVED THIS STEP FROM `policy().coverage_unbarred`, whose warning text -- *may report SATISFIED having examined any fraction of its declared scope* -- REMAINS LITERALLY TRUE OF IT. The risk persists on a surface that stopped naming it, which is worse than an unpinned step that at least still appears in the warning. ⭐ WHAT THE PIN DOES BUY, stated narrowly because the wide version was the defect: within the paths a range CHANGES, an unexamined one now BLOCKS instead of being merely reported. ⚠ NO CHECKER ASSERTS `min_coverage`. Seven axis-varied phrasings returned 18 hits, all in this file, zero in any .py and zero in guards.py -- the same standing as `scope_exclude` and `ATTRIBUTABLE`. /rely could not make the pin fire across 24 commits in three windows, because `in_scope_changed INTERSECT unexamined` was empty everywhere measured; it declined to claim the pin CANNOT fire, and so does this note. COST measured before applying and again after: blocking count 1 -> 1, +0. NOT pinned, deliberately: check_prose and check_classes (99.1%), adversary (78.7%), editorial (77.9%), prior_art (26.2%) -- pinning any of those blocks immediately.
check_claude_md.reason: the shape contract for CLAUDE.md itself, and it gates ONLY when that file is in the change -- Tim, 2026-08-26: a full re-analysis of it on every commit 'is nuts'. `when` is what makes that precise rather than a discipline: NOT_APPLICABLE on every commit that does not touch the file, REQUIRED and starting MISSING on one that does, so it fails CLOSED with nothing remembered. Registered after a measured miss -- unregistered meant V8 refused every append, the checker could never leave a key, and `inventory` never listed it, so R-NOTINLIB reached 36 lines against a 12-line cap as the largest entry in the file while '16 of 18 admission keys' read as near-complete. Same class as check_fields/RLY35-3, closed the same day. PUSH-TIME IS THE RIGHT MOMENT and that is a fact about readers, not a concession: the agent editing CLAUDE.md already holds the desired state in context, so the file's only real consumer is the NEXT session and a push is when it reaches one. NB a recorded PASS claims the two BLOCKING legs only -- rooted paths resolve, named checkers exist -- because the cap and history legs are WARN and three legs are declared PENDING and are NOT passing.

copy_editor._module_why: V20, 2026-09-08. A review step's producer is its brief. ⚠ THIS KEY WAS DELIBERATELY WITHHELD FOR SEVERAL HOURS AND THE REASON IS WORTH KEEPING, because it is the price that had to be paid before declaring was safe: `copy-editor.md` mandated THREE parallel agents recording `--step copy_editor` at one basis while carrying no V11 guidance, and V11 keys (step, basis, revision) uniquely -- reproduced against a throwaway stream, first writer APPENDED and both dissents REFUSED. Declaring the module alone would have made that broken shape appendable, which the 2026-09-08 adversary round said in terms would turn an ORDINARY finding BEDROCK the moment the key landed. ⭐ SO BOTH HALVES LANDED TOGETHER, which is what the earlier note demanded: the brief now has the CARRIER emit ONE agreement-shaped record (`--how agreement --passes 3 --agreed N`) instead of three delegated ones, so a 2-1 split is preserved as a contested UNDECIDED rather than lost to whichever agent finished first. ⚠ That route was itself unemittable until the same afternoon -- `record.py` refused `--evidence` on non-delegated routes while V21 requires a blob, so client and server closed it between them; fixed in record.py, verified by dry run returning WOULD ACCEPT. ⚠ NOTE THE RESIDUAL TENSION, unresolved on purpose: the brief's tally rule is 2-of-3 and V3 requires unanimity for a PASS under `agreement`, so the RECORD of a 2-1 split is UNDECIDED while the carrier's ESCALATION decision still follows 2-of-3. Different questions, deliberately split; if that is wrong it is Tim's call, and `copy_editor` is admitted by nothing so nothing is gated on the answer.
copy_editor._scope_is_null_deliberately: ⚠⚠ NULL WITH A REASON, NEVER A GLOB. This step's subject is a DISAGREEMENT between two states -- the adversary-passed tree and editorial's branch cut from it -- not a file set. A static path glob would rebuild exactly what made `prior_art` unsatisfiable: a TRIGGER surface that is not the REVIEW surface, so no glob expresses what a run actually covered and a file-keyed record would overclaim. PREFER NO SCOPE WITH A STATED REASON OVER A SCOPE THAT OVERCLAIMS.
copy_editor._registered_is_not_admitted: ⚠⚠ `actions: ["push"]` HERE DOES NOT GATE A PUSH, and that split is why registering now is safe. This file is the REGISTRY -- what may be RECORDED. `admission.v1.json` (gitRobot's, not ours) is the ADMISSION SET -- what must be GREEN. `copy_editor` is deliberately ABSENT from admission, so it renders in the 'registered but not gating' line and blocks nothing yet. Same shape as `prior_art` and `agent_gate`.
copy_editor._why_not_admitted_yet: ⛔ ADMISSION IS WHAT MAKES AN `UNDECIDED` BLOCK, AND THIS BRIEF HAS NEVER RUN. `UNDECIDED` is fully wired, ranks between FAIL and PASS, and has 0 records in 2,170 -- a three-editor split would be its first real use anywhere. Admitting on registration would let the first exercise of a gate nobody has watched work refuse a push. REGISTER, WATCH ONE PANEL, THEN ADMIT. The verdictLedger session owns `admission.v1.json` and will add it on request after the first run.
copy_editor.reason: the D9 copy-editor panel: THREE agents read the adversary-passed state, editorial's branch and the published prior-art references, independently, and judge whether the MEANING survived editorial's prose changes. Findings UNION across all three so a lone reader who catches a meaning shift is never outvoted; only the VERDICT is voted, 2-of-3. A split records UNDECIDED and escalates. Brief: `.claude/commands/copy-editor.md`. ⚠ `failing` is admitted on UNDECIDED precisely for this: a 2-1 split over forty files is undecided about the ONE line they disagree on and decided about the other thirty-nine, so the dispute is recorded NARROW rather than indicting the scope.

check_briefs._actions_stated_not_defaulted: ⚠ WRITTEN OUT DELIBERATELY, though it equals the default. An ABSENT `actions` key and a key naming every action are the same behaviour and different CLAIMS - one says "nobody narrowed this", the other says "all three were considered". `rely` is the measured instance: it has no key, defaults to everything, and reads a month later as a stale registry rather than a decision. DC-45 in a config file - absent and deliberate rendering identically, with the safe-looking reading being the one nobody revisits.
check_briefs.reason: the gate-brief contract: every --flag named in a record.py command line exists, every --step is REGISTERED here, every cited repo path resolves. Registered 2026-09-06 after /rely found the checker could never leave a key -- V8 refused every --record with 'step not registered', exit 2, and hooks.py rendered that refusal as 'ledger unreachable'. A checker that runs, costs time and can never record is the 'silence is never a pass' defect one layer over, same class as check_fields/RLY35-3 and check_claude_md. ⚠ A GREEN ROW CLAIMS THE THREE BLOCKING LEGS ONLY (flags, steps, paths) and their REACH IS NARROW: measured 2026-09-06, the flags leg saw 4 of 10 command flags in three briefs, steps 6 of 14 briefs, paths 15 of ~65 citations -- with 14 dead pointers in the 50 it never examined. queue/tooling-check-briefs-legs-are-narrow.md. Do not read a PASS here as 'the briefs are correct'; read it as 'nothing the legs can see is broken'.

_switches_v15: A subject set is everything the verdict DEPENDS ON, not merely everything the checker read. Found by ZeroParadox 2026-08-23: check_pov recorded 291 subjects and NOT pov_baseline.txt, so grandfathering a violation into that baseline left the record reading SATISFIED -- every file it named was unchanged. V15 refuses a record that omits a declared switch, which turns a convention into a contract: with the switch as a subject, editing a baseline moves a blob the record names, the key goes STALE, and the checker re-runs. Declaring switches is NOT a narrowing and costs no reason -- it makes a type stricter.
_vendored_allowlist_2026_08_23: vendored_files.txt switched ELEVEN checkers off and was named by none of them. Found by ZeroParadox's /rely trial: a planted DENIAL made check_pov exit 1, one appended allowlist line made it exit 0, AND NO SUBJECT MOVED. Stronger than the baseline hole of REQ-10, because an allowlist removes files from SCOPE entirely rather than grandfathering sites -- the record does not merely go unstale, the thing it covered stops existing. The count reached eleven in two passes: seven whose records already named it, then four more that had not re-recorded because none is in the pre-commit hook -- the second time that cause has hidden a set.
_approved_modules: ⛔⛔ WHICH BUILD MAY RECORD, not merely which file. `module` pins the PATH, so an EDITED checker records exactly as readily as a reviewed one. `approved_modules` lists the blob ids this step accepts, and verdictLedger's V16c REFUSES a record whose `evidence` names an unapproved build. Pinned for PUSH-GATING steps ONLY -- advisory and commit-only steps stay unpinned, so the friction is paid where publication is decided and nowhere else. ⛔⛔ WHEN A CHECKER GETS A NEW BUILD, **REPLACE** THE HASH -- DO NOT ADD TO THE LIST. `["<new>"]` is correct; `["<old>", "<new>"]` is wrong absent a stated expiry. ⚠⚠ AN ACCUMULATING LIST STOPS BEING A PIN: approve v1, v2, v3, v4 and eventually every build ever written is approved -- still LOOKING pinned while constraining nothing. That is `RLY31-6`'s exact shape, where a control decayed into permissiveness while appearing to hold and nothing was positioned to notice; this is the same trap in a different field. The history is already versioned, so every past approved set is recoverable from this file's own log -- a list inside the field duplicates that, and the duplicate is the copy that rots. Old records need no entry either: nothing re-validates the stored stream (`validate` runs only at append), so a record made under v1 stays exactly as valid as the day it landed. THE ONLY LEGITIMATE PAIR IS A ROLLOUT WINDOW -- v2 shipping while a run is in flight on v1 -- and it needs a STATED EXPIRY the way `copy_editor`'s `_why_not_admitted_yet` does, or the transitional pair quietly becomes permanent. ⭐ THE TWO-STEP COST IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS, and this was measured in the server's `inventory.py` rather than assumed: EDITING A CHECKER ALREADY STALES EVERY ROW IT PRODUCED, pinned or not -- `ev_stale` compares each record's `evidence` against current content and reports that the producer changed. So a new build means re-running that step regardless of `approved_modules`, and approving the new blob is ONE LINE IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT SHIPS THE CODE, inside a re-run you already owe. Tim's ruling on the trade: "the 'silently can't record' is the problem. fail loudly." V16c refuses naming BOTH the rejected blob and this field, and approving is a REVIEWABLE EDIT in the same history as the tool change -- the point of pinning rather than an obstacle to it. ⚠ A step with NO `approved_modules` still records; `policy()` reports `unpinned_modules`, so an unpinned step is DISCLOSED rather than silently permitted. ⚠⚠ EVERY BLOB BELOW WAS RE-DERIVED IN THIS TREE with `record.module_evidence`, the same function that computes evidence at record time, and NOT pasted from the message that proposed them. Pinning a stale blob refuses the very next run of that checker, so a copied list is the one thing this field must never contain. ⚠ THE STEP NAME IS NOT THE FILE NAME: `claim_review` pins `check_frozen.py` and `decls` pins `batch.py`. This entry's own `module` is the authority for that mapping. ⚠ IF YOU ADD A REGISTRY KEY AND IT SEEMS IGNORED: the server's `Config.requirements()` rebuilds each spec key by key from a whitelist rather than passing the entry through, so a key absent from that whitelist is invisible to every rule downstream no matter what this file says.
